senses.gloss:
लिङ्ग् लिङ्ग्, i. 1, Par. † To go.
 --i. 10 (rather a denomin. derived from लिङ्ग), Par. To change a noun according to its gender.
 --With the prep. आ आ, i. 1, Par. (in epic poetry also Ātm., Rām. 2, 64, 30), and i. 10. To embrace, Vikr. 71, 118 Mṛcch. 91, 14; Pañc. 187, 6 (i. 10); Kathās. 3, 65 (pf. red. लिलिङ्ग).
 --Ptcple. of the fut. pass. आलिङ्ग्य, n. A small drum, Rām. 5, 13, 47.
 --With प्रत्या प्रति-अ, i. 1, To return an embrace, Mṛcch. 91, 15.
 --With समा सम्-आ, i. 1,
 1. To embrace, Pañc. 27, 6; Mṛcch. 91, 13.
 2. To hold, Rām. 5, 13, 48; 53.
 --Cf. probably O.H.G. and A.S. hring; O.H.G. bringjan.

लिङ्ग लिङ्ग, n.
 1. A mark, a sign, Nal. 5, 14.
 2. A spot.
 3. A religious mark, Man. 4, 200.
 4. The penis.
 5. The phallus, or Śiva under that emblem.
 6. Nature, as the active power in creation.
 7. The primary body, Vedāntas. in Chr. 206, 11; cf. 21.
 8. Gender.
 9. The reason, or middle term, Bhāṣāp. 66.
 10. The order of the religious student.
 11. Symptom of disease.
 --Comp.
लिङ्गस्थ लिङ्ग-स्थ, m. A student in theology, Man. 8, 65.
लिङ्गालिका लिङ्गालिका, f. A small mouse or shrew.

लिङ्गिन् लिङ्गिन्, i. e. लिङ्ग + इन्,
 I. adj., f. नी,
 1. Having marks, characterised.
 2. One who is entitled to wear religious marks, Man. 4, 200.
 II. m.
 1. An ascetic, Pañc. iv. d. 41.
 2. A religious student.
 3. A worshipper of Śiva.
 4. A hypocrite.
 5. An elephant.
 --Comp.
लिङ्ग- + शरीर लिङ्ग- + शरीर, n. the primary body, Vedāntas. in Chr. 206, 21.
